about: The open sky of India, one coordinate at a time.
A whole-sky view for people, and shared infrastructure for anyone building on top of it.
Why mugilu
For years, people across India have made the sky legible one piece at a time: a map of one city's air, a thread about a heatwave, a chart of last year's monsoon.
Brilliant work, but scattered, and easy to lose by the next season.

Sathya Sankaran wanted to stop starting from scratch each time: to pull the whole sky together into one view, every hazard over any point in India, and then hand that out as infrastructure, so the next map, story or alert doesn't have to begin from nothing.
That is mugilu.
mugilu is the Kannada word for the open sky.
For people
Type a place.
See what the sky is doing to you right now: air, heat (and how survivable it really is), rain, sun and dust, alongside any official warning over that spot.
Then one plain line, the single worst thing for you, whether you have asthma, work outdoors, or are minding a child or an older parent.
No sign-up, no jargon.
Build on it
mugilu is meant to be built on, not just looked at.

Every reading is also open, machine-readable data, so you can put the whole sky behind your own map, story, dashboard or alert, and spend your time on the part that matters: the telling, and the action.
For AI agents: connect Claude, Cursor or any MCP client to /mcp; setup and the tools are on that page.
Listed in llms.txt.
For developers: a documented OpenAPI spec, and every reading as JSON or Markdown.
Embed it: a live card in one line of HTML (/embed/{lat},{lon}), or a snapshot image.
Put it on a screen: a self-refreshing wall display or kiosk for a clinic, school or lobby, set up at /display.
Add ?ref=your-site.com to any API or embed URL to have the call counted under your site's domain; no one's name is kept.
It's all free and keyless.
Where it comes from
mugilu owns no sensors and runs no forecasts.

It stands on others' work and credits them: CPCB, Airnet, Aurassure and Google AirView+ (via the OAQ broker) for air, Open-Meteo for weather, ERA5 reanalysis (Copernicus) for the heat normals, NDMA and IMD (via SACHET) for warnings, NASA FIRMS for fire smoke, JTWC for cyclone tracks, and OpenStreetMap, GeoNames and bharatlas for places and the map of India.
The code is open under the MIT licence; the data keeps each source's own terms.
Why it's free
The sky over you is a commons.
Knowing it shouldn't cost money or sit locked inside someone's app.
mugilu is non-commercial, for good: one of a growing set of free, open tools, with bharatlas and mdshare.
Common questions
Is it safe to go outside right now?
mugilu names the single worst hazard over your exact location and says plainly what to do, weighted for who you are: asthma, older adults, children, outdoor workers, or a heart condition.
It is informational, not medical or safety advice; for official warnings, consult NDMA and IMD.
What is wet-bulb temperature, and why does mugilu show it?
Wet-bulb is the temperature a wet thermometer settles at: it folds heat and humidity into the one number that decides whether your body can still cool itself.
Above about 32°C wet-bulb, even resting in shade turns dangerous.
Ordinary feels-like numbers hide this, so mugilu surfaces it.
Where does mugilu's data come from?

Air from CPCB, Airnet (CSTEP), Aurassure and Google AirView+ via the Open Air Quality (OAQ) broker; weather, heat, UV and dust from Open-Meteo, and the 1991-2020 heat normals from ERA5 reanalysis (Copernicus) via Open-Meteo; official warnings from NDMA and IMD via SACHET; fire smoke from NASA FIRMS; cyclone tracks from JTWC; place search from OpenStreetMap and GeoNames, and boundaries from bharatlas.
Each source keeps its own licence, and mugilu credits all of them.
Is mugilu free?
Yes.
It is free, open source (MIT) and non-commercial, with no sign-up.
Every reading is also available as JSON, Markdown, an embeddable card, an OpenAPI spec, and an MCP server for AI agents.
How current are the readings?
Air refreshes hourly, the national heat, rain, UV and dust grid every few hours, and official warnings hourly.
Every reading is timestamped with how long ago it was measured.
Built by urbanmorph, led by Sathya Sankaran.

methodology: How the Ambient read works
mugilu names the single worst thing the sky is doing to you right now, weighted for who you are.
It's a glass box: the thresholds below are public and come from CPCB, IMD, WHO and the Australian BoM; the smoke thresholds are mugilu's own.
Informational only, never medical or safety advice.
One read, never an average
Each hazard is scored 0–3 (low · moderate · high · severe).
We surface the worst one, named in plain words ("Severe smoke", "High heat"), with one sentence on what to do.
The other readings follow in order of risk.
Averaging would hide the thing that matters, so we never average.
For who you are
Pick a vulnerability (asthma, older adults, children, outdoor workers, heart) and the hazards that group feels more keenly are bumped up one level (so an asthmatic sees moderate air as "high").
The read then says how that group should take it ("The air is moderate. For asthma & lungs, treat it as high."), and the readings that matter to that group are tagged "for you".
When your trigger isn't the headline but is still elevated, a second line surfaces it ("also watch: air is high").
The persona is a toggle you choose: never inferred, never stored.
The thresholds
Hazard
Moderate

Smoke (fires <100 km)
UV (index)
Dust (µg/m³)
Heat takes the worst of feels-like, wet-bulb and WBGT, and the persona toggle bumps a sensitive hazard up one level.
Bands come from CPCB (air), IMD and the Australian BoM (heat / cold / wind) and WHO (UV); the smoke thresholds are mugilu's own, used only where the air is not good or satisfactory.
The full logic is the open score.ts, and every layer's source and licence is on terms & attribution.
Today against normal
On days when it stands out, the heat layer compares today's modelled high with the normal high for that place and time of year, from 1991-2020 ERA5 reanalysis (Copernicus) via Open-Meteo.
It shows only when the two are 3 °C or more apart.
It is not a heatwave declaration, which only IMD makes.

terms: Terms & attribution
mugilu stitches together others' open data for any point in India.
The stitch and the code are ours; the data is theirs, and stays under their terms.
No warranty
Informational and educational only, not for medical, emergency, or safety-critical decisions.
Readings are a mix of measured and modelled values and may be wrong, stale, or missing.
There is no accuracy or availability guarantee.
For official hazard warnings, consult NDMA and IMD directly.
Licence
The mugilu code is MIT (see the repository).
The data is not relicensed: each upstream source keeps its own licence and attribution.
mugilu is non-commercial, for individuals, and is not affiliated with any data provider.
Sources & credit
Air: CPCB (Govt. of India), Airnet (CSTEP), Aurassure, and Google AirView+, via the OAQ broker.
Modelled air, heat, rain, UV, dust, wind: Open-Meteo, licensed CC-BY 4.0.
Heat compared with normal: 1991-2020 normals from ERA5 reanalysis (Copernicus Climate Change Service), via Open-Meteo.
Official warnings: NDMA / IMD via SACHET.
Fire / crop-burn smoke: NASA FIRMS (VIIRS).
Cyclone tracks: JTWC (US Navy and Air Force).
Geography & place names: place search from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) and GeoNames (CC-BY 4.0); admin boundaries from bharatlas.
Each reading carries its own attribution line inline, so credit travels with the data wherever it goes.
Privacy
No accounts, no sign-up, no ad networks.
Usage counts are first-party and aggregate (rounded coordinates, no IP, no per-person data).
For visitor numbers and page performance, mugilu uses Cloudflare Web Analytics, which is cookieless, collects no personal data, and does no cross-site tracking or fingerprinting.
Your saved places live only in your own browser.
If you turn on alerts for a place, mugilu keeps that place (to about 1 km) and your browser's push address, only to send you official warnings for it, and deletes them when you turn alerts off.
A digital commons by urbanmorph: one of its free, open tools, with bharatlas and mdshare.
mcp: mugilu MCP server for AI assistants
Ask Claude, Cursor or any MCP client what the sky over a place in India is doing right now: air, heat, cold, rain, wind, fog, dust, smoke, UV and official warnings.
No key, no install, read only.
Connect
The server address (JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP, protocol 2025-06-18):
https://mugilu.live/mcp
Claude or Cursor: add https://mugilu.live/mcp as a custom connector.
Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http mugilu https://mugilu.live/mcp
MCP Inspector: npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli https://mugilu.live/mcp --transport http --method tools/list
Then ask, for example, "is it safe for my asthmatic kid to play outside in Indiranagar right now?"
Tools
conditions_at: What the sky is doing at a place in India RIGHT NOW (not a forecast).
search_place: Resolve an Indian place name to candidates (name, detail, coordinate).
nearest_stations: The nearest real (measured) air-quality monitoring stations to a place, with distance and current AQI.
active_warnings: Official NDMA/IMD hazard warnings currently active across India (the authoritative channel).
national_now: The national picture right now: the worst-air, hottest, and dustiest spots in India.
Every answer carries its sources and a disclaimer; please show them.
It is listed in the official MCP Registry as io.github.sathya-sankaran/mugilu.
Machine-readable: /.well-known/mcp.json and llms.txt; the code is on GitHub.
Informational only, not for medical, emergency, or safety-critical decisions.
For official warnings, consult NDMA and IMD.
